app.title: ProtoRepair
app.summary: A person uploads a protocol document (PDF, DOCX, LaTeX, text or a scanned image) or picks an example. The app extracts the text, tables and figure captions into an editable text box. The person can correct that text, then runs a fixed set of rule checks on it, with an optional model-assisted reading pass for fields the parser left missing. The app returns a three-level readiness verdict, counts of findings by severity, and a list of findings. Each finding quotes the source line, names its assumptions and evidence, and may offer one local patch, which the person can preview and re-check to see whether it clears the finding without causing a new failure. The person can also look over a derived budget table, override a few parsed values and re-run the checks, read the cited evidence, and download the full report as JSON or Markdown.

task.text: Check a written experimental protocol for unit, arithmetic and stated-limit inconsistencies before anyone carries it out, and report whether it is ready, along with proposed local fixes.

data.text: One protocol document, extracted to text with line-level steps, tables and figure captions, and parsed into a structured recipe of quantities with units. Checking it produces findings with severity, status, quote and an optional patch, plus a derived per-component budget table.
data.item: a finding raised against one step or quoted line of a protocol

stage.text: reviewing a written assembly protocol before running it at the bench

mechanism.text: A sidebar takes in a document or an example. The extracted text sits in an editable box, and buttons run the checks on it. A readiness banner with severity counts sums up the result. Tabs below show the finding cards with patch preview and re-check, the derived budget table, an override form that re-runs the checks, the evidence cards and the export buttons.

field.text: consistency checks on coin-cell assembly protocols in battery materials research

workflow.name: check a written procedure against fixed rules and propose local fixes

steps.here: Upload a PDF, DOCX, LaTeX, Markdown, text or scanned-image protocol, which is read locally into text with tables, captions and OCR. Or pick an example protocol from the sidebar.

steps.step: correct the extracted text, then compute a value from the data
steps.here: Edit the extracted text in the text box, then press 'Run deterministic checks'. Or use the optional model-assisted reading, which only fills parsed fields before the same checks run.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: A banner shows the verdict (NOT READY, REVIEW or READY), with counts of Critical, High, Medium and Low findings, fails, unknowns and proposed patches. A note explains the rule behind the verdict.

Each finding card gives its check class, status, severity, step, confidence, explanation, the quoted line, and the ids of its assumptions and evidence. Unknowns are shown as unknown rather than guessed.

steps.step: preview a proposed fix and re-check it
steps.here: Where a check has a target faithful to the source, a one-span diff patch is shown. 'Preview patched text' applies the patch and re-runs every check to confirm the target finding is gone and no new failure appeared.

The person can enter new values for loading, areal capacity, specific capacity, Li thickness and electrolyte volume in the form and re-run every check. The moisture budget tab shows the derived per-component water table and totals.
Download a JSON or Markdown report with the original text, parsed recipe, assumptions, findings, patches, evidence, readiness and missing fields. It never includes a merged protocol.

distinctive: A patch is a proposal and is never merged: one contiguous span for one finding, checked by re-running every check for target removal and new failures.
A model may only read the document into fields that pass schema and quote validation. Findings, arithmetic, patches and readiness stay with deterministic code.
Missing values stay visible as 'unknown' findings that block READY, rather than being filled in.
Every arithmetic default is listed as a named assumption, and each finding cites its assumptions and evidence ids.
A derived water and HF upper-bound budget per cell is set against component limits, with one reference line explicitly marked as not applying to this chemistry.
